replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, write the equation in standard form ax² + bx + c = 0. Then, calculate the discriminant b² - 4ac. If it's positive, you'll get two real roots; if zero, one real root; if negative, complex roots. Finally, apply the quadratic formula x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / (2a).

To find stationary points, first differentiate f(x) to get f'(x). Set f'(x) = 0 and solve for x. These x-values are critical points. Then plug them back into f(x) to find the corresponding y-values. Verify if they're maxima, minima, or points of inflection using the second derivative test.
replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: PCA reduces data dimensionality by identifying principal components that capture most variance. First, standardize your data, then compute the covariance matrix. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors reveal the directions of least variance. I wouldn't get anxious—PCA is foundational in stats and uses linear algebra concepts you can build up to gradually.
